unmapped_findings: The Ni-free alloy is labelled Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C throughout the abstract/introduction/methods/conclusions but as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C in Tables 1 and 2 (0.5 vs 0.8 C), an apparent typographical inconsistency; this sample takes the 0.8C designation.

DFT-derived lattice parameters of the κ-carbide compounds relevant to the Ni-free sample increase with Mn substitution: from 3.78 Å for Fe3AlC (Fe2MnAlC) to 3.84 Å for Mn3AlC, attributed to the larger atomic radius of Mn (rMn = 1.61 Å) vs Fe (rFe = 1.56 Å) (b0043).

DFT alternative elastic parameters: FeAl (B0 164, Cα 0.54, G 81.5, E100 210, E111 333), Fe3Al (153, 0.12, 21, 60, 322), Fe3AlC(sp) (216, 2.39, 175, 477, 217), Mn3AlC (B0 −214, Cα −1.59, G −175, E100 −412, E111 −285) — Table 4 (b0064). The Fe3AlC phase shows the largest bulk modulus and strong anisotropy (Cα > 1), while FeAl shows a low degree of anisotropy.

The presence of Mn in Fe3AlC-κ increases its elastic constants (Mn3AlC > Fe3AlC), and the shear modulus of Fe3AlC is greater than FeAl or Fe3Al, confirming the un-shearable nature of κ precipitates and the experimentally observed hardening of Mn-enriched κ (b0054, b0056).
